leading_positions.synthesis: Four of the eight round-1 configurations prefer Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks, each with the same two names. They share the view that the magic-wavelength idea plus the many-atom Lamb-Dicke architecture is a distinct invention reproduced across laboratories and species at about 1e-18, and that the two-name credit is the cleanest on the shortlist. Their citations differ in emphasis: Johansson and Kroll stress invention and development at the 1e-18 level (Kroll adds frequency comparison), Lindroth stresses trapping at the magic wavelength for accuracy and stability, and Olsson stresses the magic-wavelength trap and a fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. All four list the same open points: the claims of Takamoto, Ido and Lemonde, how much of Ye's credit rests on earlier comb and laser-stabilisation work, and overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes. Johansson moved here from circuit QED in the preferred configuration citing his own circuit-QED connection as a reason. Lindroth explicitly warns that agreement among members with an atomic-physics vantage is not itself evidence of merit. Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig and Pearce list B042 as an alternative or fallback in their files, but do not prefer it.

Danielsson alone prefers the ATLAS and CMS Higgs discovery with Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee. His case is that nature answered a half-century question, that the 2013 prize recognised only the theoretical mechanism, and that maturity is not in doubt. He concedes that the trio is a leadership proxy for thousands of people, that spokespersons or analysis leaders could be argued instead, and that if no defensible three names exist the committee should turn elsewhere. Other members describe the science as decisive but object to the attribution basis (Johansson, Mehlig, Lindroth, Eriksson, Kroll, Olsson); Pearce calls it an acceptable fall-back. Lindroth would reconsider if a defensible attribution principle emerges, and Mehlig would support it if the committee explicitly accepts the leadership proxy.

Pearce alone prefers IceCube with Halzen and Spiering, arguing it is a discovery of nature that opened neutrino astronomy through a kilometre-scale detector, with a two-name credit that avoids the leadership-proxy problem. Danielsson, Lindroth and Olsson accept the flux as secure but see the astrophysical interpretation and source identification as still developing, and all raise the credit boundary with Baikal, DUMAND, AMANDA and ANTARES. Pearce himself lists partial source identification and the narrower support as weaknesses and names B042 as his first alternative. Danielsson ranks it as a strong alternative and would support Halzen and Spiering.

Eriksson alone prefers room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and MgO junctions with Miyazaki, Moodera and Parkin, on the grounds that the physics is closed (symmetry-selective tunnelling predicted and confirmed), three decades of replication, and industrial impact. He identifies the open points himself: Yuasa and Djayaprawira are outside the trio for the coherent-MgO step, and the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize may be seen as covering the territory. Olsson regards the attribution gap as affecting the main step of the story and places it behind clocks, and Johansson says he has not ranked it. No other member prefers it, and Eriksson notes he cannot treat that as a verdict on merit.

Mehlig alone prefers Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality with Kardar, Zhang and Takeuchi, on the strength of the exact connections to random-matrix statistics and the precise liquid-crystal experimental confirmation. He states the weaknesses against his own choice: Parisi's co-authorship of the 1986 paper, the exact-solution contributors outside the trio, a narrow experimental base, and no technological anchor. Eriksson says KPZ lies outside his expertise. Mehlig says he would be comfortable with B042 as a compromise if B034 cannot gather support.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members agree that the Higgs discovery is of exceptional scientific importance; objections to B026 concern attribution, not merit.
Every member who states a view on the sequence treats lattice-clock maturity as well established: independent confirmation across laboratories and species at about 1e-18 is not disputed in any file.

Maturity of IceCube diffuse flux and of the 2018 twisted-bilayer-graphene experiments is accepted, while the interpretation of source origin and of superconductivity respectively is described as still developing by several members.

All eight files treat B042 with Katori and Ye as at least a serious option: four prefer it with the identical pair of names, and the other four (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Pearce) name it as an alternative or fallback.

Several members, from different fields, say that a three-person limit forces explicit decisions on who is omitted, and that the citation should be written to claim no more than the credited names delivered.

Members consistently say that the 2005 frequency-comb prize, the 2012 prize on control of single quantum systems, the 2013 Higgs theory prize, the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize, the 2016 topological-phases prize and the 2025 macroscopic-quantum-circuits prize bear on how new candidates are framed.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a new principle (the many-atom, light-shift-cancelled lattice) or an incremental refinement of capabilities honoured in 2005 and 2012. Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Johansson and Mehlig (conditionally) accept the first reading; Pearce prefers an observational channel he regards as new, and Danielsson says precision metrology does not answer a question comparable to the origin of mass.
Whether a discovery of nature (Higgs, IceCube) should weigh more than an invention that improves a measurement (clocks), and whether that criterion should drive the choice at all.

Whether the astrophysical interpretation of IceCube (population origin of the diffuse flux, a single compelling blazar association) is settled enough to treat the discovery as complete, as against Pearce's view that it is mature enough to stand.
Whether the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize covers the same territory as tunnel magnetoresistance, as against Eriksson's statement that the mechanism is distinct.
Whether KPZ universality has the physical reach, beyond a few experimental systems, to carry a prize, given that only Mehlig prefers it.
attribution_disputes: B026: whether the founding proposers and leaders Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are a defensible proxy for thousands of collaborators, or whether spokespersons or analysis leaders at the time of discovery have an equal or better claim. Danielsson, Mehlig, Johansson, Lindroth, Eriksson, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce all address this and none identifies a settled basis.

B042: whether the prize is for the concept (Katori) and record performance (Ye), and how to treat the first Sr lattice-clock demonstration by Takamoto and Ido and the contributions of Lemonde, Ludlow and others, all outside the credited names. Kroll and Johansson would confine Ye's credit to the lattice clock and keep the thorium nuclear clock out of the citation, and Kroll and Olsson raise the same question about his comb and ultrastable-laser work.

B029: how to word a citation fair to Baikal, DUMAND, AMANDA and ANTARES pioneers while naming only Halzen and Spiering, and whether the size of the IceCube Collaboration makes a two-name prize contestable.
B037: whether the coherent-MgO step credited to Yuasa and Djayaprawira is covered by the supplied trio.
B007: Eriksson and Johansson note that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal) and the 3D pioneers are outside the Kane, Mele and Molenkamp trio.
B034: Parisi's co-authorship and the exact-solution contributors are outside the credited trio.
B054: Yuan Cao, the experimental lead of the 2018 results, is outside the credited names.
B033: Johansson and Mehlig propose different three-name subsets of the four credited names, differing on Girvin versus Blais.

B010 and B053: members propose differing laureate triples that overlap on Zoller (Eriksson and Mehlig: Bloch, Greiner, Zoller; Kroll: Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger) and on the trapped-ion versus optical-lattice split.
maturity_disputes: Whether the pending redefinition of the second should affect timing of B042. Olsson says a prize for the invention should not wait for a metrological decision; Kroll and Johansson say the citation should rest on what has been demonstrated and not on the redefinition; Danielsson rejects framing the redefinition as imminent.
Whether IceCube source identification is advanced enough (Danielsson, Lindroth, Olsson raise it; Pearce accepts it as a reservation).
Whether twisted bilayer graphene should wait for a resolved pairing mechanism: Danielsson, Mehlig and Pearce say wait, Eriksson now treats it as promising but early.
Whether a close follow-on to the 2025 circuit prize is premature for circuit QED, raised by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Mehlig.
Whether the topological-insulator case is clear after the 2016 prize, raised by Eriksson, Johansson and Olsson.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Pearce (chair) discloses co-authorship of the Fermi-LAT instrument paper and membership of PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and PoGO+; Fermi-LAT observations were part of the TXS 0506+056 multi-messenger follow-up relevant to B029. He describes it as a collaboration-level, not personal, link and leaves the question of recusal to the committee.

Johansson discloses work in circuit and waveguide QED, direction of WACQT at Chalmers, and close Chalmers links to Delsing, Wilson and Kockum; he would consider recusal on B033, which he no longer prefers.

Kroll discloses a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, adjacent to the field of B042 although with no documented tie to Katori or Ye, and flags ties to Lund colleagues, WACQT and Deep Light Vision that bear on B053 and quantum-memory or quantum-computing candidates.

Olsson discloses long-running exchanges with Japanese universities including a University of Tokyo fellowship, with Katori Tokyo-based but no documented tie to him or to Ye; she also notes Johansson is a Chalmers colleague.
Danielsson discloses two years at CERN in the early 1990s, before ATLAS and CMS were built, with no documented tie to Della Negra, Jenni or Virdee.
Eriksson notes that B037 lies close to his field of theoretical magnetism, with no documented connection to Moodera, Parkin or Miyazaki.
Mehlig notes that his background in random matrices and stochastic dynamics could make him a partial judge of B034.
Lindroth reports no conflict for B042 and discloses collaborations with the Lund attosecond group, ETH Zurich and others that would matter only for an attosecond ballot.
questions_for_round2: For B042: should the citation rest on the magic-wavelength lattice concept, on the demonstrated 1e-18 performance, or on both, and how should Takamoto, Ido and Lemonde be handled if only Katori and Ye are named? Can members who consider the lattice clock an incremental step beyond the 2005 and 2012 prizes state which specific new principle would or would not satisfy them?

For B026: can any member state a principle for choosing three names (founding proposers and leaders, spokespersons at discovery, or analysis leaders) and say concretely what each named person contributed to the 2012 observation? If none can, should B026 be set aside on attribution grounds despite undisputed scientific weight?

For B029: can a citation naming Halzen and Spiering be worded fairly to Baikal, DUMAND, AMANDA and ANTARES, and does the evidence for the diffuse flux plus the TXS 0506+056 association make the discovery sufficiently settled? Is the chair's flagged Fermi-LAT link grounds for him to recuse on this ballot?

For B037: do members who did not rank tunnel magnetoresistance now accept that it is distinct from giant magnetoresistance, and can Eriksson state whether Yuasa and Djayaprawira should replace one of the three names?
For the single-member preferences (B034, B029, B037, B026): will any other member support one of these configurations, and what evidence would let non-specialists assess them?

For B054 and B007: if the committee wishes to look beyond these, what new evidence would settle the pairing mechanism and the omission of Cao for B054, and the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang for B007?

How should the committee weigh agreement among members with an atomic-physics vantage on B042 against the objection that it may reflect a shared disciplinary bias, and do members outside AMO regard the conceptual step as substantial?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows one position preferred by four of the eight members (B042 with Katori and Ye) and four positions each preferred by a single member (B026, B029, B037, B034). The clock case has the cleanest explicit credit but faces overlap and priority questions, while the Higgs case is not disputed scientifically and is limited by attribution, and the IceCube case depends on source maturity and on pioneer credit. Several members list B042 as an alternative while preferring a different case, so the second round should test whether the single-member preferences can be supported or whether the committee converges on a configuration without a decisive scientific objection. The chair notes his own disclosed connection to B029 and takes no view on the outcome here.
